previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, mechanical mitral valve on anticoagulation, functioning pancreas transplant, and systolic heart failure was admitted for supratherapeutic INR of 10.6 and acute-on-chronic anemia, following transfer from an outside hospital. She had experienced mild chest pain attributed to demand ischemia from low hemoglobin, which resolved after blood transfusion and nitroglycerin. She received one unit of FFP and two units of packed red blood cells during her stay. INR initially dropped to 2.3 despite continued warfarin, prompting a short heparin bridge, which was discontinued once INR returned to therapeutic range. Warfarin was adjusted from 5 mg to 2.5 mg daily. She underwent scheduled hemodialysis, which helped manage acidosis and overall stability. The anemia was attributed to ongoing lower gastrointestinal oozing, with no acute intervention required. She remained stable, asymptomatic at discharge, and was sent home with services and close follow-up for INR monitoring.

microbiology.comments: NEGATIVE FOR CMV IgM ANTIBODY BY EIA.  INTERPRETATION:  INFECTION AT UNDETERMINED TIME.  A positive IgG result generally indicates past exposure.  Infection with CMV once contracted remains latent and may reactivate when immunity is compromised.  Greatly elevated serum protein with IgG levels >2000 mg/dl may cause  interference with CMV IgM results.  If current infection is suspected, submit follow-up serum in 2-3 weeks.
